paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: : Loss steps
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the loss values across iterations for five different models: Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64, H/T), and SepLLM (n=128). The x-axis, labeled "#Iteration," represents the number of iterations and ranges from 0 to 140,000 with a scale that appears to be linear, marked at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis, labeled "Loss," represents the loss value and ranges from 2.4 to 3.4, also on a linear scale. All five lines start at a high loss value of approximately 3.4 at iteration 0 and exhibit a sharp initial decrease. The "Vanilla" model (purple line) shows the fastest initial drop, stabilizing around a loss of 2.6 by iteration 20,000. The "StrmLLM (n=64)" (blue line), "SepLLM (n=64)" (orange line), "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" (green line), and "SepLLM (n=128)" (dark blue line) all follow a similar trend, with the "SepLLM (n=128)" line showing a slightly higher loss than the others after the initial drop. After the initial steep decline, all models converge to a stable loss value of approximately 2.5 to 2.6 by iteration 140,000. The "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" and "SepLLM (n=128)" lines are very close to each other, indicating similar performance. The "StrmLLM (n=64)" line is consistently above the "SepLLM" lines after the initial drop, suggesting a slightly higher loss. The "Vanilla" line is consistently below the other lines after the initial drop, indicating a lower loss. The lines are relatively flat after the initial drop, indicating that the models have converged.
